records.source: Ἦν δὲ τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὰ ἄζυμα μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας.
records.gloss: It was now the Passover and the Unleavened [Bread] after two days.
pieces: Two days remained before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

L.1: Now it was the Passover and the [Feast of] Unleavened Bread after two days.

R.1: In two more days it would be time for the Passover and the Festival of Unleavened Bread.

decisions.choice: the Passover and Unleavened Bread: one festival week
decisions.reason: The Passover meal was eaten on the night of 15 Nisan and was followed by seven days of eating bread without yeast (Exodus 12:1-20; Leviticus 23:5-6). By this time the two names were used together for the whole festival.

decisions.choice: after two days: two days from now
alternatives: two full days later, on the third day
decisions.reason: The phrase counts forward from the time Mark is describing; it places the plot of 14:1-2 just before the feast.

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread
decisions.reason: Readable uses "festival", an everyday word for a holy feast.

records.heading: A plot two days before the Passover

records.source: καὶ ἐζήτουν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς πῶς αὐτὸν ἐν δόλῳ κρατήσαντες ἀποκτείνωσιν, ἔλεγον γάρ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, μήποτε ἔσται θόρυβος τοῦ λαοῦ.
records.gloss: And were seeking the chief priests and the scribes how him by deceit having seized they might kill. \v 2 They were saying for, Not during the feast, lest there will be an uproar of the people.
pieces: The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by a trick and put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.
For they kept saying, "Not at the feast, in case the people raise an uproar."

L.1: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by deceit [and] kill [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}].
L.2: For they were saying, "Not during the feast, or there will be an uproar of the people."

R.1: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law were trying to find a secret way to arrest Jesus and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.2: They said, "We must not do it during the festival. The crowds might start a riot."

decisions.choice: by deceit: by a trick, out of public view
decisions.reason: The word means cunning or treachery. They want to seize Jesus quietly, away from the crowds who listened to him gladly (12:37).

decisions.choice: the feast: Passover week, when Jerusalem was full of pilgrims
alternatives: the meal on the first night only
decisions.reason: Large crowds came for the festival, and the Romans feared unrest at this time. An arrest in public could start a riot.

decisions.choice: they were saying: they kept saying among themselves
alternatives: they said it once in public
decisions.reason: The tense describes talk that went on while they made their plans.

decisions.choice: leading priests; teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: The same Readable terms as in earlier chapters.

records.source: Καὶ ὄντος αὐτοῦ ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ κατακειμένου αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν γυνὴ ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου νάρδου πιστικῆς πολυτελοῦς· συντρίψασα τὴν ἀλάβαστρον κατέχεεν αὐτοῦ τῆς κεφαλῆς.
records.gloss: And being him in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, reclining him, came a woman having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil of nard pure, very costly; having broken the alabaster flask she poured [it] on his head.
pieces: Jesus was in Bethany, at the home of Simon the leper. While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lay at the meal, a woman came with an alabaster flask of pure nard, a perfumed oil of great value. She broke the flask and poured the oil over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

L.3: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table], a woman came having an alabaster flask of perfumed oil, pure nard, very costly; breaking the alabaster flask, she poured [it] over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

R.3: Jesus was in the town of Bethany, eating a meal at the home of Simon. Simon had once had a bad skin disease. A woman came in with a jar made of fine white stone. It was full of very costly perfume made from nard. She broke the jar open and poured the perfume on Jesus' head.

decisions.choice: reclining: lying on a couch at a meal
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on their left side around a low table, with their feet away from it.

decisions.choice: alabaster flask of pure nard: a sealed stone flask of costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a soft white stone used for flasks of perfume. Nard was an oil made from a plant that grows in the Himalayas, so it was rare and very costly. The flask was often sealed, so it was broken at the neck to pour out the oil.

decisions.choice: pure: genuine, not mixed with cheaper oils
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its meaning is not certain. The most likely sense is "genuine" or "pure", from a word for trust.

decisions.choice: poured over his head: an anointing like that of a king
decisions.reason: Kings were anointed on the head (1 Samuel 10:1; 2 Kings 9:6). Jesus himself gives the act another meaning in 14:8: it prepares his body for burial.

decisions.choice: the leper (B); had once had a bad skin disease (R)
alternatives: a man with a serious skin disease
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the name by which Simon was known. Readable says what it meant, as in 1:40, and says "had once had" because he was clearly no longer shut out from others. That is an inference.

decisions.choice: a jar made of fine white stone
decisions.reason: Readable explains what alabaster is.

records.heading: Anointed at Bethany

records.source: ἦσαν δέ τινες ἀγανακτοῦντες πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη τοῦ μύρου γέγονεν;
records.gloss: Were now some being indignant among themselves: For what this waste of the perfumed oil has happened?
pieces: Some of those present were angry and said to one another, "What is the point of wasting this perfume?

L.4: Now there were some who were indignant among themselves, "Why has this waste of the perfumed oil happened?

R.4: Some of the people there became angry. They said to each other, "Why did she waste that perfume?

decisions.choice: some: some of those at the meal
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were. Matthew 26:8 says the disciples, and John 12:4 names Judas.

decisions.choice: among themselves: to one another, or within themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean they spoke among themselves or felt it inwardly. Since their words are given and they rebuke her in 14:5, they seem to have said it to one another.

decisions.choice: waste: loss, something thrown away
decisions.reason: The word means ruin or loss. To them the oil was simply lost.

records.source: ἠδύνατο γὰρ τοῦτο τὸ μύρον πραθῆναι ἐπάνω δηναρίων τριακοσίων καὶ δοθῆναι τοῖς πτωχοῖς· καὶ ἐνεβριμῶντο αὐτῇ.
records.gloss: Could for this the perfumed oil have been sold for more than denarii three hundred and have been given to the poor. And they were scolding her.
pieces: It could have fetched more than {{units:a year's wages|300 denarii}}, and the money could have gone to the poor." So they turned on her with harsh words.

L.5: For this perfumed oil could have been sold for more than 300 denarii and given to the poor." And they were scolding her.

R.5: It could have been sold for more than {{units:a year's pay|300 denarii}}. Then the money could have been given to poor people." And they spoke angrily to her.

decisions.choice: 300 denarii: about a year's pay for a worker
decisions.reason: A denarius was a day's wage for a laborer (Matthew 20:2). Three hundred denarii was close to what a worker earned in a year, leaving out Sabbaths and feast days.

decisions.choice: given to the poor: gifts to the poor were expected at Passover
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:11), and it was the custom to give to them at Passover.

decisions.choice: scolding: speaking sternly, with anger
decisions.reason: The verb is the strong one used in 1:43. It means to speak to someone harshly.

decisions.choice: a year's wages (B); a year's pay (R); 300 denarii as the original unit
decisions.reason: The units setting gives a modern sense of the sum by default and the coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the coin.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἄφετε αὐτήν· τί αὐτῇ κόπους παρέχετε;
records.gloss: But Jesus said, Leave her alone; why to her troubles are you causing?
pieces: But Jesus said, "Let her be. Why are you bothering her?

L.6: But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you causing her trouble?

R.6: But Jesus said, "Stop bothering her. Why are you giving her a hard time?

decisions.choice: causing her troubles: making things hard for her
decisions.reason: The phrase means to bother or harass someone.

decisions.choice: leave her alone: stop what you are doing to her
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "forgive", but here it means to let her be.

records.source: καλὸν ἔργον ἠργάσατο ἐν ἐμοί·
records.gloss: A good work she did to me.
pieces: She has done a beautiful thing for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.6: She has done a good work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.6: What she did for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} was very good.

decisions.choice: a good work: a fine, fitting deed
decisions.reason: The adjective means good and also fine or beautiful. Jewish teaching counted burying the dead among good works, beyond giving to the poor, and 14:8 links her act to burial.

decisions.choice: beautiful
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the sense of something fine and fitting, not only right.

records.source: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν, καὶ ὅταν θέλητε δύνασθε αὐτοῖς εὖ ποιῆσαι, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·
records.gloss: Always for the poor you have with yourselves, and whenever you want you are able to them well to do, me but not always you have.
pieces: The poor will be with you at all times, and you can help them any time you wish. But you will not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.7: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them, but you do not always have {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.7: There will always be poor people near you. You can help them whenever you want to. But I will not always be here with you.

decisions.choice: you always have the poor with you: an echo of Deuteronomy 15:11
alternatives: a saying that the poor do not matter
decisions.reason: The law says the poor will never cease from the land, and so Israel must open its hand to them. Jesus does not set aside that duty. He says there will be time for it.

decisions.choice: you will not always have me: Jesus speaks of his coming death
alternatives: he is going on a journey
decisions.reason: The words point ahead to 14:8 and to his death within days.

decisions.choice: I will not always be here with you
alternatives: you do not always have me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the words mean in plain terms.

records.source: ὃ ἔσχεν ἐποίησεν, προέλαβεν μυρίσαι τὸ σῶμά μου εἰς τὸν ἐνταφιασμόν.
records.gloss: What she had she did; she took beforehand to anoint my body for the burial.
pieces: She did what was in her power. She has poured perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body ahead of time, to make it ready for burial.

L.8: She has done what she could; she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body beforehand for burial.

R.8: She did what she was able to do. She put perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body to get it ready to be buried. She did it before the time came.

decisions.choice: what she had she did: she did what she could
decisions.reason: The phrase means she did all that lay in her power.

decisions.choice: she took beforehand to anoint: she anointed ahead of time
decisions.reason: The verb "take beforehand" with another verb means to do something in advance.

decisions.choice: for burial: the anointing looks ahead to Jesus' death
alternatives: she knew he was about to die
decisions.reason: Bodies were anointed for burial. In 16:1 the women come to anoint his body and find the tomb empty, so this is the only anointing his body receives. Mark does not say whether she understood this.

records.source: ἀμὴν δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη λαληθήσεται εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: Truly now I say to you, wherever is proclaimed the gospel in the whole world, also what did this [woman] will be spoken for a memorial of her.
pieces: Truly I tell you, in every place in the whole world where the gospel is proclaimed, people will tell what she has done, and remember her."

L.9: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her."

R.9: I tell you the truth: The good news will be preached in the whole world. And everywhere it is preached, people will tell what this woman did, and they will remember her."

decisions.choice: the gospel: the good news about Jesus
alternatives: one of the four written Gospels
decisions.reason: As in 1:1 and 13:10, the word means the message about Jesus, not a book.

decisions.choice: will be spoken: will be told
decisions.reason: The passive leaves open who tells it; those who proclaim the gospel will tell her story with it.

decisions.choice: for a memorial of her: so that she is remembered
alternatives: a memorial before God, like an offering
decisions.reason: The word can mean an offering that reminds God (Acts 10:4), but here it means that people will remember her.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as elsewhere in Mark.

records.source: Καὶ Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριὼθ ὁ εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδοῖ αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And Judas Iscariot, the one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests so that him he might hand over to them.
pieces: Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went off to the chief priests to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to them.

L.10: And Judas Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve, went away to the chief priests in order to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to them.

R.10: Then Judas Iscariot went to the leading priests. He was one of Jesus' twelve followers. He went to offer to help them arrest Jesus.

decisions.choice: hand over: give Jesus up to his enemies, a betrayal by a friend
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, and it is the word Jesus used of his own coming death (9:31; 10:33). When Judas is the subject, it means betrayal.

decisions.choice: the one of the Twelve: one of the Twelve, as everyone knew
decisions.reason: The article may point to him as the one already known from 3:19. Mark stresses that the betrayer was one of Jesus' closest followers.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B); help them arrest (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that links this to Jesus' sayings about being handed over. Balanced and Readable name the betrayal.

records.heading: Judas goes to the chief priests

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ἐχάρησαν καὶ ἐπηγγείλαντο αὐτῷ ἀργύριον δοῦναι.
records.gloss: And having heard they rejoiced and promised him silver to give.
pieces: They were delighted to hear it and promised to pay him.

L.11: And when they heard [it], they rejoiced and promised to give him money.

R.11: The priests were very happy when they heard this. They promised to give Judas money.

decisions.choice: silver: money
decisions.reason: The word means silver and was used of money in general. Matthew 26:15 gives the sum as thirty pieces of silver.

decisions.choice: they rejoiced: the leaders' problem of 14:1-2 is solved
decisions.reason: One of Jesus' own followers offers a way to take him quietly.

records.source: καὶ ἐζήτει πῶς αὐτὸν εὐκαίρως παραδοῖ.
records.gloss: And he was seeking how him conveniently he might hand over.
pieces: So Judas looked for a good chance to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: And he was seeking how he might conveniently hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.

R.11: From then on Judas watched for the right time to hand Jesus over to them.

decisions.choice: conveniently: at a good moment, when no crowd was near
decisions.reason: The leaders wanted to avoid the crowds (14:2), so Judas looked for a time when Jesus was away from them.

decisions.choice: betray (B); hand ... over to them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the betrayal as in 14:10. Readable spells out to whom he was handed over.

records.source: Καὶ τῇ πρώτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν ἀζύμων, ὅτε τὸ πάσχα ἔθυον, λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ· Ποῦ θέλεις ἀπελθόντες ἑτοιμάσωμεν ἵνα φάγῃς τὸ πάσχα;
records.gloss: And on the first day of the Unleavened [Bread], when the Passover they were sacrificing, say to him the disciples of him, Where do you want having gone we should prepare so that you may eat the Passover?
pieces: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the day the Passover lambs were sacrificed, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where would {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} like us to go and make ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover meal?"

L.12: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover [lamb], {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want us to go and prepare for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to eat the Passover?"

R.12: It was the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. On this day the lambs were killed for the Passover meal. Jesus' followers said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where should we go to make the Passover meal ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: say: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, past events are told in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past: they asked. Mark does the same many times in this chapter.

decisions.choice: the first day ... when they sacrificed the Passover: 14 Nisan
alternatives: 15 Nisan, the day after the meal
decisions.reason: The lambs were killed in the temple on the afternoon of 14 Nisan and eaten that evening, when 15 Nisan began. People also spoke of 14 Nisan as the first day of the festival, because all yeast was removed from houses that day.

decisions.choice: the Passover: the Passover meal, with its lamb
decisions.reason: Here the word means the meal, as "eat the Passover" shows.

decisions.choice: the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the meal is meant.

records.heading: Preparing the Passover

records.source: καὶ ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἄνθρωπος κεράμιον ὕδατος βαστάζων· ἀκολουθήσατε αὐτῷ, καὶ ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθῃ εἴπατε τῷ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅτι Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ποῦ ἐστιν τὸ κατάλυμά μου ὅπου τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου φάγω;
records.gloss: And he sends two of the disciples of him and says to them, Go into the city, and will meet you a man a jar of water carrying; follow him, \v 14 and wherever he enters say to the master of the house that The Teacher says, Where is the guest room of me where the Passover with the disciples of me I may eat?
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent off two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples with these instructions: "Go into the city. A man carrying a water jar will come to meet you. Follow him,
and when he goes into a house, tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Which is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room, where I am to eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'

L.13: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and says to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him,
L.14: and wherever he goes in, say to the owner of the house, 'The Teacher says, "Where is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} guest room where I may eat the Passover with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} disciples?"'

R.13: Jesus sent two of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers into Jerusalem. He told them, "Go into the city. You will meet a man who is carrying a jar of water. Follow him.
R.14: He will go into a house. Say to the owner of that house, 'The Teacher wants to know, "Where is the room for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to stay in? I want to eat the Passover meal there with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} followers."'

decisions.choice: a man carrying a jar of water: an unusual sight that would stand out
decisions.reason: Women usually carried water in jars; men carried it in skins. A man with a jar would be easy to pick out.

decisions.choice: Jesus' knowledge of what will happen
alternatives: only a plan made in advance with the owner
decisions.reason: Mark tells this as in 11:2-6: things happen as Jesus says. Whether Jesus had arranged it beforehand or foresaw it, Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: guest room: a room where guests lodge or eat
decisions.reason: The word is the one used at Luke 2:7. It means a lodging or guest room in a house.

decisions.choice: the Teacher: Jesus, as his followers called him
alternatives: a title the owner gave him
decisions.reason: The owner seems to know who "the Teacher" is, which suggests he was a follower or friend.

decisions.choice: into Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city.

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμῖν δείξει ἀνάγαιον μέγα ἐστρωμένον ἕτοιμον· καὶ ἐκεῖ ἑτοιμάσατε ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: And he you will show an upper room large, furnished, ready; and there prepare for us.
pieces: He himself will show you a big upper room, set out with couches and ready. Get things ready for us there."

L.15: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished [and] ready; and prepare [it] for us there."

R.15: He will show you a large room upstairs. It will have everything you need. Get the meal ready for us there."

decisions.choice: furnished: spread with couches and cushions for a meal
decisions.reason: The word means spread or laid out. In a dining room it means the couches were in place for reclining at the meal.

decisions.choice: he himself: the owner of the house
decisions.reason: The pronoun is emphatic and points back to the owner of 14:14.

decisions.choice: set out with couches
decisions.reason: Balanced says what furnishing a dining room meant.

records.source: καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.
records.gloss: And went out the disciples and came into the city and found as he said to them, and they prepared the Passover.
pieces: So the disciples set out, came into the city and found it all as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and there they prepared the Passover.

L.16: And the disciples went out and came into the city and found [it] just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had told them, and they prepared the Passover.

R.16: The two followers went into the city. Everything happened just as Jesus had told them. So they got the Passover meal ready there.

decisions.choice: prepared the Passover: had the lamb killed at the temple and readied the meal
decisions.reason: Getting the meal ready meant taking the lamb to the temple to be sacrificed, roasting it, and setting out unleavened bread, bitter herbs and wine.

decisions.choice: the two followers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the two sent in 14:13 are meant.

records.source: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἔρχεται μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.
records.gloss: And evening having come he comes with the Twelve.
pieces: When evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} arrived with the Twelve.

L.17: And when evening came, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes with the Twelve.

R.17: That evening Jesus came to the house with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve followers.

decisions.choice: evening: the Passover meal was eaten at night
decisions.reason: The law says the lamb is eaten that night (Exodus 12:8). With sunset 15 Nisan began.

decisions.choice: came to the house with his twelve followers
decisions.reason: Readable says where he came and who the Twelve were.

records.heading: One of you will hand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over

records.source: καὶ ἀνακειμένων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσθιόντων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με ὁ ἐσθίων μετ’ ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: And reclining them and eating, Jesus said, Truly I say to you that one of you will hand over me, the [one] eating with me.
pieces: As they lay at the table and ate, Jesus told them, "Truly I tell you, one of you here, eating with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.18: And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "Truly I say to you that one of you will hand {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over, the one who is eating with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.18: While they were eating, Jesus said, "I tell you the truth: one of you will betray {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He is eating here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} now."

decisions.choice: the one eating with me: an echo of Psalm 41:10
alternatives: only a description of where he sat
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of a close friend "who ate my bread" lifting his heel against the psalmist. To betray someone you had eaten with was a deep wrong.

decisions.choice: hand over: betray
decisions.reason: As in 14:10, the verb used of Judas means betrayal.

decisions.choice: hand over (L); betray (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same choice as in 14:10.

records.source: ἤρξαντο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ εἷς κατὰ εἷς· Μήτι ἐγώ;
records.gloss: They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, Surely not I?
pieces: They were deeply hurt, and one after another they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "It is not I, is it?"

L.19: They began to be grieved and to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} one by one, "Surely not I?"

R.19: The followers became very sad. One after another, they asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "You do not mean me, do you?"

decisions.choice: surely not I?: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is put in a form that hopes for "no". Each one wants to be told it is not he.

decisions.choice: Surely not I?, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Surely not I? And another, Surely not I?
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and another said, Surely not I?". The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: You do not mean me, do you?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in everyday words that keep its hopeful tone.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ ἐμβαπτόμενος μετ’ ἐμοῦ εἰς τὸ τρύβλιον·
records.gloss: But he said to them, One of the Twelve, the [one] dipping with me into the bowl.
pieces: He said to them, "It is one of the Twelve, one who dips bread into the bowl with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.20: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "[It is] one of the Twelve, the one who is dipping with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} into the bowl.

R.20: Jesus answered, "It is one of you twelve. He is dipping his bread into the same bowl as I am.

decisions.choice: dipping into the bowl: sharing the same dish of sauce at the meal
alternatives: a sign that points out one man
decisions.reason: At the Passover meal bread and herbs were dipped into a shared bowl of sauce. Jesus does not name the man; the words stress that the betrayer is a close companion.

decisions.choice: dipping: now, at this meal
decisions.reason: The present participle describes one who shares the meal now, not one who will dip next.

decisions.choice: his bread
decisions.reason: Readable says what was dipped.

records.source: ὅτι ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ δι’ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.
records.gloss: For indeed the Son of Man goes as it has been written concerning him, woe but to the man that through whom the Son of Man is handed over; good for him if not had been born the man that.
pieces: The Son of Man is going as it stands written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but how terrible for the man who betrays the Son of Man! It would be good for that man if he had never been born."

L.21: For the Son of Man goes just as it has been written about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! [It would be] good for him if that man had not been born."

R.21: The Son of Man will die, just as the Scriptures say. But how terrible it will be for the man who betrays {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! That man would be better off never being born."

decisions.choice: goes: goes to his death
decisions.reason: To "go" is a way of speaking of death. Jesus' death follows the path set out in Scripture.

decisions.choice: as it has been written: the Scriptures about the suffering of God's servant
decisions.reason: Mark does not name a passage. Texts such as Isaiah 53 and Psalm 22 speak of a righteous sufferer (see 9:12).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning
decisions.reason: The word mourns what is coming upon the man and warns of it at the same time.

decisions.choice: God's plan and human guilt together
alternatives: Judas only did what was fated
decisions.reason: The death is foretold in Scripture, but the one who betrays Jesus is still held responsible.

decisions.choice: betrays (B, R)
decisions.reason: Where the one through whom it happens is Judas, Balanced and Readable name the betrayal. Literal keeps "handed over".

decisions.choice: will die, just as the Scriptures say
alternatives: goes as it is written about him
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "goes" means and what is written.

records.source: Καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Λάβετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.
records.gloss: And eating them, having taken bread, having blessed, he broke and gave to them and said, Take; this is the body of me.
pieces: During the meal {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took bread, spoke the blessing, broke it and handed it to them, saying, "Take it. This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

L.22: And as they were eating, taking bread [and] blessing [God], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [it] and gave [it] to them and said, "Take; this is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

R.22: While they were eating, Jesus took some bread and thanked God for it. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke it, gave it to them, and said, "Take this. It is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} body."

decisions.choice: having blessed: having said the blessing over the bread, which praises God
decisions.reason: A Jewish blessing at a meal praised God who brings bread from the earth. The blessing is addressed to God, as the thanks over the cup in 14:23 is.

decisions.choice: this is my body: the bread is given as Jesus himself, given up in death
alternatives: only a picture with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Christians have understood these words in different ways. The text gives the words as Jesus said them, with the link to his death that 14:24 makes plain.

decisions.choice: Take, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "eat", as in Matthew 26:26. The earliest manuscripts have "Take" alone. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: thanked God for it
decisions.reason: Readable says what the blessing was.

records.heading: My body, my blood of the covenant

records.source: καὶ λαβὼν ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἔπιον ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες.
records.gloss: And having taken a cup, having given thanks, he gave to them, and they drank from it all.
pieces: He also took a cup, and after giving thanks {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} passed it to them, and every one of them drank from it.

L.23: And taking a cup [and] giving thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave [it] to them, and they all drank from it.

R.23: Then Jesus took a cup of wine. He thanked God for it and gave it to them. All of them drank some of it.

decisions.choice: a cup: a cup of wine at the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Wine was drunk at the Passover meal. Jewish writings from a little later speak of four cups through the evening. Mark does not say which cup this was.

decisions.choice: giving thanks: thanking God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used at the feeding of the four thousand (8:6). From it comes the later name Eucharist.

decisions.choice: a cup of wine
decisions.reason: Readable says what was in the cup, as 14:25 shows.

records.source: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν.
records.gloss: And he said to them, This is the blood of me of the covenant, the [blood] being poured out for many.
pieces: He said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood of the covenant, poured out for many.

L.24: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.

R.24: Jesus said to them, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood. It puts God's covenant into effect. It is poured out for many people.

decisions.choice: blood of the covenant: Exodus 24:8
alternatives: a new phrase with no background
decisions.reason: At Sinai Moses sprinkled the people with blood and said, "See the blood of the covenant." Jesus' blood seals a covenant as the sacrifice at Sinai did.

decisions.choice: the covenant, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "the new covenant", as in Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. The earliest manuscripts do not have "new". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: poured out for many: an echo of Isaiah 53:12 and Mark 10:45
decisions.reason: The servant of Isaiah 53 "poured out his life to death" and bore the sin of many. "Many" stresses the great number; it does not mean that some are left out.

decisions.choice: being poured out: a present that looks to what is about to happen
decisions.reason: His blood is about to be shed. The present makes the coming death certain.

decisions.choice: It puts God's covenant into effect
decisions.reason: Readable says what "blood of the covenant" means: blood that makes the covenant binding.

records.source: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐκέτι οὐ μὴ πίω ἐκ τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: Truly I say to you that no longer not not I will drink of the fruit of the vine until the day that when it I drink new in the kingdom of God.
pieces: Truly I tell you, I will never again drink the fruit of the vine until the day I drink it new in the kingdom of God."

L.25: Truly I say to you that I will no longer drink at all of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."

R.25: I tell you the truth: I will not drink wine again until the day when I drink new wine in God's kingdom."

decisions.choice: the fruit of the vine: wine
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from the Jewish blessing over wine.

decisions.choice: no longer ... not at all: a strong denial
decisions.reason: Greek here piles up negatives to make the denial as strong as possible.

decisions.choice: new in the kingdom of God: at the feast when God's rule has fully come
decisions.reason: "New" points to a new kind of life. The prophets pictured God's rule as a great banquet (Isaiah 25:6). Jesus looks beyond his death to that day.

decisions.choice: wine; new wine
alternatives: the fruit of the vine; it new
decisions.reason: Readable names the wine and says plainly what will be new.

records.source: Καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.
records.gloss: And having sung a hymn they went out to the Mount of the Olives.
pieces: Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.

L.26: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

R.26: Then they sang a song of praise to God and went out to the Mount of Olives.

decisions.choice: a hymn: the psalms of praise sung at the close of the Passover meal
decisions.reason: Psalms 113-118, called the Hallel, were sung at Passover, the last part at the end of the meal. Mark does not say which song they sang.

decisions.choice: the Mount of Olives: the hill east of Jerusalem
alternatives: a hill far from the city
decisions.reason: During the festival pilgrims were to stay within the area of greater Jerusalem, which included this hill across the Kidron valley.

decisions.choice: a song of praise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

records.source: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πάντες σκανδαλισθήσεσθε, ὅτι γέγραπται· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα διασκορπισθήσονται.
records.gloss: And says to them Jesus that All you will fall away, because it has been written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.
pieces: Jesus told them, "All of you will stumble and fall away, for it stands written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'

L.27: And Jesus says to them, "You will all fall away, because it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'

R.27: Then Jesus told them, "Every one of you will turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The Scriptures say, 'I will strike down the shepherd, and the sheep will run off in all directions.'

decisions.choice: fall away: be tripped up so as to desert him
decisions.reason: The verb means to stumble or be caused to sin. Here it means they will desert Jesus when he is arrested (14:50), not that they will be lost for good, as 14:28 shows.

decisions.choice: I will strike the shepherd: Zechariah 13:7
decisions.reason: In Zechariah God calls for the sword to strike his shepherd so that the sheep scatter. Mark gives it in the first person, "I will strike", which makes plain that God is the one acting.

decisions.choice: I: God himself
decisions.reason: Jesus' enemies do the deed, but the death takes place within God's purpose.

decisions.choice: turn away from me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what falling away means here.

records.heading: Peter's denial foretold

records.source: ἀλλὰ μετὰ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
records.gloss: But after the being raised me I will go before you into the Galilee.
pieces: But after I am raised up, I will lead the way ahead of you into Galilee."

L.28: But after I have been raised, I will go before you into Galilee."

R.28: But after God raises {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from death, I will go to Galilee before you get there."

decisions.choice: being raised: raised by God
decisions.reason: The verb is passive in form. In the New Testament God is the one who raises Jesus. Some take the form as simply "rise"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: go before: go ahead of, as a shepherd leads his flock
decisions.reason: After the picture of the scattered sheep, Jesus promises to gather them again. The angel at the tomb repeats the promise (16:7).

decisions.choice: God raises me from death
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raises, as the passive implies.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἔφη αὐτῷ· Εἰ καὶ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται, ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐγώ.
records.gloss: But Peter said to him, If even all will fall away, yet not I.
pieces: Peter told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "They may all fall away, but I will not."

L.29: But Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Even if all fall away, yet not I."

R.29: Peter said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "All the others may turn away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, but I never will!"

decisions.choice: even if all ...: Peter sets himself apart from the rest
alternatives: he doubts the others will fall
decisions.reason: Peter grants that the others might fail but says he will be the exception.

decisions.choice: all the others
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Peter means the other disciples.

records.source: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι σὺ σήμερον ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἢ δὶς ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ.
records.gloss: And says to him Jesus, Truly I say to you that you today this night before twice a rooster crows three times me you will deny.
pieces: Jesus answered him, "Truly I tell you, before a rooster crows twice today, this very night, you yourself will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."

L.30: And Jesus says to him, "Truly I say to you that you, today, this night, before a rooster crows twice, will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times."

R.30: Jesus answered, "I tell you the truth: Tonight, before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: today, this night: the day began at sunset
decisions.reason: A Jewish day ran from evening to evening, so the night already begun was part of "today".

decisions.choice: before a rooster crows twice: before the early hours of the morning
decisions.reason: Roosters crow in the night as well as at dawn. The time of their crowing was a name for the third watch of the night (13:35).

decisions.choice: twice, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: before a rooster crows, without twice
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts do not have "twice", here or at 14:68 and 14:72, which brings Mark into line with the other Gospels. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: deny: disown, say he does not know Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter's three denials in 14:68-71 show what is meant: he says he does not know Jesus. Compare 8:34, where following Jesus means to deny oneself.

decisions.choice: say three times that you do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the denial will be.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐκπερισσῶς ἐλάλει· Ἐὰν δέῃ με συναποθανεῖν σοι, οὐ μή σε ἀπαρνήσομαι.
records.gloss: But he emphatically was saying, If it is necessary me to die with you, not not you I will deny.
pieces: But Peter kept saying all the more firmly, "Should I have to die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, still I will never deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.31: But he kept saying emphatically, "If I must die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I will never deny {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.31: But Peter said it again and again, very strongly, "I will never say I do not know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! I will die with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} if I have to!"

decisions.choice: emphatically: with great force, more and more
decisions.reason: The adverb is very strong, and the verb is continuous: he kept on insisting.

decisions.choice: not not I will deny: never will I deny
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the strongest denial Greek can make.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ πάντες ἔλεγον.
records.gloss: Likewise and also all were saying.
pieces: And every one of them said the same.

L.31: And they all were also saying the same.

R.31: All the other followers said the same thing.

decisions.choice: all were saying: all the disciples said so too
decisions.reason: All of them make the promise that all will break in 14:50.

records.source: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς χωρίον οὗ τὸ ὄνομα Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Καθίσατε ὧδε ἕως προσεύξωμαι.
records.gloss: And they come to a place of which the name [is] Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples of him, Sit here while I pray.
pieces: Then they came to a place by the name of Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Stay seated here while I pray."

L.32: And they come to a place whose name [is] Gethsemane, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Sit here while I pray."

R.32: They went to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, "Sit here while I go and pray."

decisions.choice: Gethsemane: a name meaning "oil press"
decisions.reason: The name comes from the Hebrew and Aramaic for an olive press. It was an olive grove on the Mount of Olives; John 18:1 calls it a garden.

decisions.choice: a place: a piece of land, an estate
decisions.reason: The word means a plot of ground or a small property.

decisions.choice: go and pray
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jesus goes on a little way to pray, as 14:35 says.

records.heading: Gethsemane

records.source: καὶ παραλαμβάνει τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἤρξατο ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε.
records.gloss: And he takes Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be greatly alarmed and to be distressed, \v 34 and he says to them, Very sorrowful is the soul of me to death; remain here and keep watch.
pieces: He took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and horror and anguish came over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
He said to them, "My soul is filled with grief, grief enough to die. Wait here and stay awake."

L.33: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} takes Peter and James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to be greatly alarmed and distressed,
L.34: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "My soul is very sorrowful, even to death. Remain here and keep watch."

R.33: Jesus took Peter, James and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He began to feel great fear and deep pain.
R.34: He said to them, "My heart is so full of sorrow that I feel as if I am dying. Stay here and keep watch."

decisions.choice: greatly alarmed and distressed: overwhelmed with horror and anguish
decisions.reason: The first verb is the strong word for being overwhelmed used in 9:15 and 16:5-6. The second means to be in deep distress. Together they show Jesus in agony as he faces his death.

decisions.choice: my soul is very sorrowful: words from Psalms 42 and 43
decisions.reason: The refrain "Why are you cast down, my soul?" (Psalm 42:6, 42:12; 43:5) uses this word in the Greek version. Jesus prays in the words of a psalm of distress.

decisions.choice: even to death: sorrow so great it could kill
decisions.reason: The phrase measures the grief: it is deep enough to bring death (compare Jonah 4:9).

decisions.choice: keep watch: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 13:34-37 for servants who must stay awake for their master's coming.

decisions.choice: My heart is so full of sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the inner self.

records.source: καὶ προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπιπτεν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ προσηύχετο ἵνα εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν παρέλθῃ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἡ ὥρα, καὶ ἔλεγεν· Αββα ὁ πατήρ, πάντα δυνατά σοι· παρένεγκε τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ· ἀλλ’ οὐ τί ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλὰ τί σύ.
records.gloss: And having gone forward a little he was falling on the ground and was praying that if possible it is might pass from him the hour, \v 36 and he was saying, Abba, the Father, all things [are] possible to you; take away the cup this from me; but not what I will but what you.
pieces: He went on a little way, threw {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to the ground and prayed that the hour might pass {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} by, if that could be.
He said, "Abba, Father, for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} all things are possible. Remove this cup from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Yet let it be what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will, not what I will."

L.35: And going forward a little, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was falling on the ground and praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying, "Abba, Father, all things [are] possible for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Take this cup away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but not what I will, but what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [will]."

R.35: Jesus went a short way farther. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell to the ground and prayed. He asked that, if it could happen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not have to go through this time of suffering.
R.36: He said, "Abba, Father, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything. Please take this cup of suffering away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, not what I want."

decisions.choice: was falling ... was praying ... was saying: prayer that went on
decisions.reason: The verbs are continuous. Jesus prayed this way again and again (14:39).

decisions.choice: Abba, Father: the Aramaic word for father, with its Greek meaning
decisions.reason: Abba was the word a son or daughter used for their father, at any age. Mark keeps it and adds the Greek word. Paul says that believers too cry "Abba, Father" (Romans 8:15; Galatians 4:6).

decisions.choice: the hour; this cup: the suffering and death now upon him
decisions.reason: The cup is a picture from the prophets of God's judgment that must be drunk (Isaiah 51:17; Jeremiah 25:15). Jesus used it in 10:38-39. The hour is the time of his betrayal and death (14:41).

decisions.choice: not what I will but what you will: Jesus gives his will over to the Father's
decisions.reason: Jesus asks for the cup to be taken away, but puts the Father's will first. He does what he taught in 3:35 and 8:34.

decisions.choice: this time of suffering; this cup of suffering
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hour and the cup stand for.

records.source: καὶ ἔρχεται καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Σίμων, καθεύδεις;
records.gloss: And he comes and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter, Simon, are you sleeping?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you asleep?

L.37: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes and finds them sleeping, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping?

R.37: Then Jesus came back and found the three followers asleep. He said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping?

decisions.choice: Simon: Peter's own name, not the name Jesus gave him
alternatives: no meaning in the change of name
decisions.reason: Since 3:16 Mark has called him Peter. Jesus now uses his old name. Some see a hint that he is not living up to his new name; Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: comes, finds, says: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present again; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the three followers
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the three of 14:33 are meant.

records.source: οὐκ ἴσχυσας μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι;
records.gloss: Not were you strong one hour to keep watch?
pieces: Did you not have the strength to stay awake a single hour?

L.37: Were you not strong enough to keep watch one hour?

R.37: Could you not stay awake for just one hour?

decisions.choice: were you strong: you, Peter alone
decisions.reason: The verb is singular. Peter, who had promised so much (14:29-31), could not stay awake for one hour.

decisions.choice: strong: able, having the strength
decisions.reason: The verb means to have strength for something.

records.source: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ ἔλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
records.gloss: Keep watch and pray, so that not you come into temptation; the indeed spirit [is] willing, but the flesh weak.
pieces: Stay awake and pray that you will not come into temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."

L.38: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not come into temptation; the spirit indeed [is] willing, but the flesh [is] weak."

R.38: Stay awake and pray. Then you will not give in when temptation comes. Your spirit wants to do what is right, but your body is weak."

decisions.choice: keep watch and pray: now spoken to all three
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural. Jesus turns from Peter to all of them.

decisions.choice: temptation: a time of testing that could lead them to fall
alternatives: an inward desire for something wrong only
decisions.reason: The word means a test or trial. The arrest is about to test them, and they will fall (14:50). Compare the prayer "lead us not into temptation" (Matthew 6:13).

decisions.choice: the spirit and the flesh: the willing human spirit and weak human nature
decisions.reason: The spirit here is the inner self that wants to do right; the flesh is human nature in its weakness. Some take the spirit as God's Spirit, but the contrast is within the person.

decisions.choice: your spirit wants to do what is right; your body
alternatives: the spirit is willing; the flesh
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying in plain words.

records.source: καὶ πάλιν ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπών.
records.gloss: And again having gone away he prayed the same word having said.
pieces: He went away again and prayed, using the same words.

L.39: And again going away, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} prayed, saying the same word.

R.39: Jesus went away again and prayed the same prayer.

decisions.choice: the same word: the same request
decisions.reason: The word can mean a saying or a matter. Jesus prayed the same prayer as before.

records.source: καὶ πάλιν ἐλθὼν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ καταβαρυνόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδεισαν τί ἀποκριθῶσιν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And again having come he found them sleeping, were for of them the eyes being weighed down, and not they knew what they might answer him.
pieces: Coming back again, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them asleep; they could not keep their eyes open, and they had no answer to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.40: And again coming, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what they should answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.40: Jesus came back to them again. Once more {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found them sleeping. They were too tired to keep their eyes open. They did not know what to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: eyes weighed down: very drowsy
decisions.reason: The phrase means they were heavy with sleep.

decisions.choice: did not know what to answer: they were ashamed and had nothing to say
decisions.reason: As on the mountain in 9:6, the disciples are at a loss for words.

records.source: καὶ ἔρχεται τὸ τρίτον καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἀπέχει· ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα, ἰδοὺ παραδίδοται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰς τὰς χεῖρας τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν.
records.gloss: And he comes the third [time] and says to them, Are you sleeping the rest and resting? It is enough; came the hour, look, is handed over the Son of Man into the hands of the sinners.
pieces: He came a third time and said to them, "Still asleep? Still resting? Enough of that! The hour is here. See, the Son of Man is being handed over into the power of sinners.

L.41: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes the third [time] and says to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough. The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.

R.41: Jesus came back a third time and said to them, "Are you still asleep and resting? That is enough! The time is here. Look! The Son of Man is being handed over to sinful people.

decisions.choice: Are you still sleeping and resting?: a question
alternatives: Sleep on now and take your rest (a command)
decisions.reason: The same words can be read as a command, said with sorrow or irony: "Sleep on, then." But the next words wake them up, so a question fits better.

decisions.choice: it is enough: that is enough, the time for sleep is over
decisions.reason: The word is unclear here. In business it meant "paid in full", and some take it of Judas receiving his money. The most common reading is "enough!". Some manuscripts add words to explain it.

decisions.choice: handed over: given up by God's plan, through Judas's betrayal
decisions.reason: This is the word of Jesus' sayings about his death (9:31; 10:33). Here it covers both what Judas does and what God allows.

decisions.choice: sinners: those who act against God, here his enemies
decisions.reason: The word may point to the Gentiles who will kill him (10:33), but the arresting crowd comes from the Jewish leaders.

decisions.choice: into the power of
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the idiom.

records.source: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ὁ παραδιδούς με ἤγγικεν.
records.gloss: Rise, let us go; look, the [one] handing over me has drawn near.
pieces: Get up; we must go. Look, the one who betrays {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is near."

L.42: Rise, let us go. Look, the one who is handing {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} over has drawn near."

R.42: Get up! Let us go. Look! The man who is betraying {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is almost here."

decisions.choice: let us go: let us go to meet them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not flee. He goes out to meet those who come for him.

decisions.choice: has drawn near: is here
decisions.reason: The perfect means he has come near and is now at hand, as in 1:15.

decisions.choice: the one who betrays (B); the man who is betraying (R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Balanced and Readable name Judas's act as betrayal.

records.source: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος παραγίνεται Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων.
records.gloss: And immediately, yet him speaking, arrives Judas one of the Twelve and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
pieces: Right then, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still talking, Judas came up, one of the Twelve. A crowd came with him carrying swords and clubs. They had been sent by the chief priests, the scribes and the elders.

L.43: And immediately, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

R.43: Just then, while Jesus was still speaking, Judas arrived. He was one of the twelve followers. A crowd came with him. They had swords and heavy sticks. The leading priests, the teachers of God's law, and the elders had sent them.

decisions.choice: a crowd ... from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders: men sent by the council
decisions.reason: The three groups make up the council of 14:53-55. Those sent were likely the temple guard and servants of the high priest (14:47).

decisions.choice: one of the Twelve: Mark repeats it
decisions.reason: Mark names him again in this way (as in 14:10 and 14:20) to stress that the betrayer was one of Jesus' own.

decisions.choice: clubs: wooden staves
decisions.reason: The word means wood and is used of clubs or cudgels.

decisions.choice: right then (B); just then (R)
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Literal says "immediately" and the other levels vary the phrase.

records.heading: Arrested with a kiss

records.source: δεδώκει δὲ ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν σύσσημον αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπάγετε ἀσφαλῶς.
records.gloss: Had given now the [one] handing over him a signal to them saying, Whomever I kiss, he is; seize him and lead away securely.
pieces: Judas, the betrayer, had given them a signal beforehand. "The one I kiss is {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}," he had said. "Take hold of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and lead {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away under close guard."

L.44: Now the one who was handing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over had given them a signal, saying, "Whomever I kiss, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is [the one]; seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and lead [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away under guard."

R.44: Judas had told them ahead of time how they would know which man was Jesus. He said, "The man I kiss is the one you want. Grab {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away. Guard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} well."

decisions.choice: kiss: the usual greeting of a disciple to his teacher
decisions.reason: A kiss was a common greeting of respect. Judas turns that greeting into a signal, and in the dark the crowd needs to know which man to take.

decisions.choice: securely: under guard, so that he does not escape
decisions.reason: The word can mean safely or securely. Judas wants to make sure Jesus is held.

decisions.choice: signal: an agreed sign between people
decisions.reason: The word means a token agreed beforehand.

decisions.choice: Judas, the betrayer, had given them a signal beforehand
alternatives: the one handing him over had given them a signal
decisions.reason: Balanced names Judas and makes clear the signal was arranged in advance, as the past perfect implies.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθὼν εὐθὺς προσελθὼν αὐτῷ λέγει· Ῥαββί, καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And having come immediately having approached him he says, Rabbi, and kissed him.
pieces: As soon as he arrived, he went straight up to Jesus and said, "Rabbi!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.45: And coming, immediately approaching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, he says, "Rabbi," and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.45: Judas came and went straight to Jesus. He said, "Teacher!" and kissed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: my teacher, a respectful title
decisions.reason: Judas greets Jesus with the title of honor a disciple used for his teacher (9:5; 11:21).

decisions.choice: kissed: the stronger form of the verb
decisions.reason: The verb is a compound of the one in 14:44. It may mean he kissed him warmly, which makes the betrayal worse, or it may simply mean kissed.

decisions.choice: Teacher
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, Readable says "Teacher" for Rabbi.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἐπέβαλαν τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: And they laid the hands on him and seized him.
pieces: They then laid hands on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} prisoner.

L.46: And they laid hands on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and seized {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.46: Then the men grabbed Jesus and arrested {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: laid hands on: took hold of by force
decisions.reason: Here laying on hands is an arrest, not a blessing.

records.source: εἷς δέ τις τῶν παρεστηκότων σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἔπαισεν τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον.
records.gloss: One but a certain of those standing by, having drawn the sword, struck the slave of the high priest and took off of him the ear.
pieces: But one of the bystanders pulled out his sword, hit the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.

L.47: But a certain one of those standing by drew his sword, struck the slave of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

R.47: One of the people standing there pulled out a sword. He swung it at the high priest's servant and cut off his ear.

decisions.choice: a certain one of those standing by: Mark does not name him
decisions.reason: John 18:10 names Peter and the slave, Malchus. Mark leaves him unnamed. He seems to be one of Jesus' followers.

decisions.choice: slave: one owned by the high priest, here likely one of his trusted men
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. A high priest's slave could hold a position of trust.

decisions.choice: ear: the whole ear or the earlobe
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for ear, but such forms were often used with no sense of smallness.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με;
records.gloss: And answering Jesus said to them, As against a bandit did you come out with swords and clubs to capture me?
pieces: Jesus said to them, "Have you come with swords and clubs to seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as you would a bandit?

L.48: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you come out with swords and clubs to capture {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as against a bandit?

R.48: Jesus said to them, "Do you think I am a robber? Is that why you came with swords and clubs to arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: bandit: a robber or armed rebel
alternatives: a thief who steals in secret
decisions.reason: The word is used of violent robbers and of rebels against Rome. Jesus is crucified between two of them (15:27).

decisions.choice: a question
alternatives: a statement: you have come out as against a bandit
decisions.reason: The sentence can be read as a statement or a question. Read either way, Jesus protests at the way they treat him.

decisions.choice: Do you think I am a robber? Is that why ...?
alternatives: As against a bandit did you come out ...?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two to make the point clear.

records.source: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἤμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με· ἀλλ’ ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαί.
records.gloss: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and not you seized me; but so that may be fulfilled the Scriptures.
pieces: Day after day I was among you in the temple, teaching, and you did not lay a hand on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But this is happening so that the Scriptures would be fulfilled."

L.49: Every day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; but [this has happened] so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."

R.49: Day after day I taught in the temple area, right there with you. You did not arrest {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} then. But all this is happening to make the Scriptures come true."

decisions.choice: but so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled: words are left out
alternatives: Let the Scriptures be fulfilled (a command)
decisions.reason: The sentence is cut short. It may mean "this has happened so that ..." or work as a wish: "let the Scriptures be fulfilled." The sense is the same: these events are in God's plan.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures: such as Zechariah 13:7 and Isaiah 53:12
decisions.reason: Jesus does not name a passage. He quoted Zechariah 13:7 in 14:27, and Isaiah 53:12 says the servant was counted with rebels.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts, where he taught in 11:27-12:44
decisions.reason: Jesus taught in the open courts of the temple area.

records.source: καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον πάντες.
records.gloss: And having left him they fled all.
pieces: And they all left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran.

R.50: Then all of Jesus' followers left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and ran away.

decisions.choice: they all fled: what Jesus foretold in 14:27
decisions.reason: The sheep are scattered as Zechariah 13:7 said, and the "all" who promised in 14:31 all run.

decisions.choice: all of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who fled.

records.source: Καὶ νεανίσκος τις συνηκολούθει αὐτῷ περιβεβλημένος σινδόνα ἐπὶ γυμνοῦ, καὶ κρατοῦσιν αὐτόν, ὁ δὲ καταλιπὼν τὴν σινδόνα γυμνὸς ἔφυγεν.
records.gloss: And a young man certain was following with him, having wrapped a linen cloth around [his] naked [body], and they seize him; \v 52 but having left behind the linen cloth naked he fled.
pieces: A certain young man had been going along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with only a linen sheet thrown around his bare body. They seized him,
but he slipped out of the linen sheet and ran away naked.

L.51: And a certain young man was following with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having wrapped a linen cloth around [his] naked [body], and they seize him;
L.52: but leaving behind the linen cloth, he fled naked.

R.51: A young man was following Jesus. He was wearing only a linen cloth. The men grabbed him.
R.52: But he left the cloth in their hands and ran away with no clothes on.

decisions.choice: a certain young man: Mark does not say who he was
decisions.reason: Only Mark tells this. Some have guessed the young man was Mark, but the text gives no name and there is no evidence.

decisions.choice: fled naked: possibly an echo of Amos 2:16
decisions.reason: Amos says that on the day of judgment even the bravest will flee away naked. Whether Mark had this in mind is not certain; the scene shows that even the last follower fled.

decisions.choice: linen cloth: a sheet or wrap of linen
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the cloth in which Jesus is buried (15:46).

decisions.choice: they seize: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present; the sense is past.

records.source: Καὶ ἀπήγαγον τὸν Ἰησοῦν πρὸς τὸν ἀρχιερέα, καὶ συνέρχονται πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς.
records.gloss: And they led away Jesus to the high priest, and come together all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
pieces: Jesus was led off to the high priest's house, where all the chief priests, elders and scribes came together.

L.53: And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.

R.53: The men took Jesus to the house of the high priest. All the leading priests, the elders, and the teachers of God's law met together there.

decisions.choice: the high priest: Caiaphas, high priest at this time
decisions.reason: Mark does not name him. Matthew 26:57 names Caiaphas, who held the office from about AD 18 to 36.

decisions.choice: all the chief priests, elders and scribes: the members of the council
decisions.reason: The three groups made up the council, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem (14:55). They meet at night, in the high priest's house.

decisions.choice: come together: present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Mark's vivid present; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the house of the high priest
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him, as 14:54 shows.

records.heading: Before the council

records.source: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ἕως ἔσω εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ ἦν συγκαθήμενος μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν καὶ θερμαινόμενος πρὸς τὸ φῶς.
records.gloss: And Peter from a distance followed him as far as inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the light.
pieces: Peter kept well back, but followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the way inside the high priest's courtyard. He sat down among the guards and warmed himself by the firelight.

L.54: And Peter followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from a distance, right inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.

R.54: Peter followed Jesus, but he stayed far behind. He went into the yard of the high priest's house. He sat with the guards and warmed himself by the fire.

decisions.choice: the light: the fire, whose light showed his face
decisions.reason: The word means light. Here it is a fire, and its light lets the servant girl see him (14:67).

decisions.choice: officers: attendants of the council, the temple guards
decisions.reason: The word means assistants or attendants; here they are the guards who served the high priest.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the open court inside a large house
decisions.reason: Large houses were built around an open court.

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον ἐζήτουν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μαρτυρίαν εἰς τὸ θανατῶσαι αὐτόν, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον·
records.gloss: And the chief priests and all the Council were seeking against Jesus testimony in order to put to death him, and not they were finding.
pieces: Meanwhile the chief priests and the entire Council searched for testimony against Jesus that would let them have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} executed, but they could not find any.

L.55: Now the chief priests and the whole Council were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, and they were not finding [any].

R.55: The leading priests and the whole Jewish council tried to find people who would say something against Jesus. They wanted a reason to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But they could not find any.

decisions.choice: the Council: the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court
decisions.reason: The council in Jerusalem had seventy-one members under the high priest and judged matters of Jewish law.

decisions.choice: testimony: the evidence of witnesses
decisions.reason: The law required the word of two or three witnesses for a sentence of death (Deuteronomy 17:6).

decisions.choice: they had decided on the end first
decisions.reason: Mark shows that they were looking for evidence to fit a verdict already reached (14:1).

decisions.choice: the whole Jewish council
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Council was, as in 15:1.

records.source: πολλοὶ γὰρ ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἴσαι αἱ μαρτυρίαι οὐκ ἦσαν.
records.gloss: Many for were bearing false witness against him, and alike the testimonies not were.
pieces: Plenty of people testified falsely against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but what they said did not match.

L.56: For many were bearing false witness against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and their testimonies were not consistent.

R.56: Many people told lies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But their stories did not agree with each other.

decisions.choice: not alike: not consistent, not agreeing
decisions.reason: Under the law two witnesses had to agree on the facts (Deuteronomy 19:15). These did not, so their word could not stand.

decisions.choice: false witnesses: an echo of the psalms of the righteous sufferer
decisions.reason: Psalm 27:12 and Psalm 35:11 speak of false witnesses rising up against the righteous.

records.source: καί τινες ἀναστάντες ἐψευδομαρτύρουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἡμεῖς ἠκούσαμεν αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἐγὼ καταλύσω τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον τὸν χειροποίητον καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ἄλλον ἀχειροποίητον οἰκοδομήσω·
records.gloss: And some having stood up were bearing false witness against him saying \v 58 that We heard him saying that I will destroy the temple this the made with hands and in three days another not made with hands I will build.
pieces: Then some of them got up and brought a false charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:
"We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} declare, 'I will pull down this temple that human hands have made, and in three days I will put up another that no hands have made.'"

L.57: And some stood up and were bearing false witness against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying,
L.58: "We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saying, 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.'"

R.57: Then some people stood up and told this lie about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:
R.58: "We heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say, 'I will tear down this temple that people built. Then in three days I will build a different one, which people do not build.'"

decisions.choice: false witness: Jesus had not said he would destroy the temple
decisions.reason: Jesus foretold that the temple would be destroyed (13:2), but Mark calls this report false. John 2:19 has a saying about the temple of his body, which may lie behind it.

decisions.choice: made with hands; not made with hands: human-made and made by God
alternatives: built of stone; built of wood
decisions.reason: "Made with hands" was often said of idols and of things that are only human (Acts 7:48). A temple not made with hands would be God's own work.

decisions.choice: another temple: a new place of God's presence
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain it. Christians later saw in it Jesus' risen body or the community of his people, but Mark leaves it as the witnesses' charge.

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word here is the one for the sanctuary building, not the whole temple area of 14:49.

records.source: καὶ οὐδὲ οὕτως ἴση ἦν ἡ μαρτυρία αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And not even thus alike was the testimony of them.
pieces: But even on this point what they said did not match.

L.59: And even so their testimony was not consistent.

R.59: But even these people did not tell the same story.

decisions.choice: not even thus: not even on this charge
decisions.reason: Even the temple saying could not be used, because the witnesses did not agree.

records.source: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἰς μέσον ἐπηρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν;
records.gloss: And having stood up the high priest in the middle questioned Jesus saying, Not you answer nothing?
pieces: The high priest rose, stepped into the middle and put a question to Jesus: "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer at all?

L.60: And the high priest stood up in the middle and questioned Jesus, saying, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer nothing?

R.60: Then the high priest stood up in front of everyone. He asked Jesus, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not going to answer?

decisions.choice: two questions: Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?
alternatives: one question: Do you answer nothing to what these testify against you?
decisions.reason: The words can be read as one question or two. The SBLGNT makes them two sentences.

decisions.choice: in the middle: in the center of the council
alternatives: in the middle of the night
decisions.reason: The council sat in a half circle; the high priest steps forward to question the accused.

records.source: τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;
records.gloss: What these you testify against?
pieces: What is this that these people are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

R.60: What about all these things they are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: what are these testifying: what do you say to their charges?
alternatives: what are they saying (he did not hear)
decisions.reason: The high priest asks Jesus to answer the charges.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐσιώπα καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο οὐδέν.
records.gloss: But he was silent and not answered nothing.
pieces: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept silent and made no answer at all.

L.61: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was silent and answered nothing.

R.61: But Jesus said nothing. He did not answer at all.

decisions.choice: he was silent: an echo of Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant of the LORD was led like a lamb to slaughter and did not open his mouth.

decisions.choice: not ... nothing: not a word
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the silence complete.

records.source: πάλιν ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ εὐλογητοῦ;
records.gloss: Again the high priest was questioning him and says to him, You are the Christ the Son of the Blessed?
pieces: Again the high priest put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Son of the Blessed One?"

L.61: Again the high priest was questioning {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of the Blessed [One]?"

R.61: The high priest asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the Son of God, the Blessed One?"

decisions.choice: the Blessed: God
decisions.reason: Jews spoke of God with titles like "the Blessed One" out of reverence for his name.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of the Blessed: the anointed king, God's Son
decisions.reason: The two titles name one figure. The king from David's line was called God's son (2 Samuel 7:14; Psalm 2:7). Mark opened his book with both titles (1:1).

decisions.choice: You: emphatic
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: you, this prisoner, the Messiah?

decisions.choice: the Son of God, the Blessed One
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom the title means.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι, καὶ ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ δεξιῶν καθήμενον τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον μετὰ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
