records.gloss: And Jesus said, I am, and you will see the Son of Man at the right [hand] sitting of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.
pieces: Jesus said, "I am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven."

L.62: And Jesus said, "I am, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."

R.62: Jesus said, "Yes, I am. And you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of God, the Mighty One. You will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming with the clouds of heaven."

decisions.choice: I am: yes, I am the Messiah, the Son of God
alternatives: only the divine name of Exodus 3:14
decisions.reason: The words answer the question directly. Some hear an echo of God's name, as at 6:50, but the plain sense is yes.

decisions.choice: I am, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "You say that I am", which is like Matthew 26:64 and Luke 22:70. Nearly all have "I am". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the right hand of the Power; coming with the clouds: Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: Psalm 110:1 has the Lord tell the king to sit at his right hand; Daniel 7:13 sees one like a son of man coming with the clouds to God. Jesus joins them, as he did in 12:36 and 13:26. In the Psalm the Hebrew has the divine name, the LORD.

decisions.choice: the Power: God
decisions.reason: Another reverent title for God, like "the Blessed One" in 14:61.

decisions.choice: God, the Mighty One; You will see him
decisions.reason: Readable names God, adds "yes" to make the answer plain, and splits the long sentence in two.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀρχιερεὺς διαρρήξας τοὺς χιτῶνας αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων;
records.gloss: And the high priest having torn the tunics of him says, What still need have we of witnesses?
pieces: The high priest ripped his clothes. "What more do we need witnesses for?

L.63: And the high priest, tearing his garments, says, "What further need do we have of witnesses?

R.63: The high priest tore his clothes to show his horror. He said, "We do not need any more witnesses!

decisions.choice: tearing his garments: a sign of horror at hearing blasphemy
decisions.reason: Tearing clothes showed grief or horror (2 Kings 18:37). Later Jewish rules say judges did this on hearing blasphemy.

decisions.choice: garments: tunics, the clothes worn under the cloak
alternatives: the high priest's robes of office
decisions.reason: The word is plural; men of rank might wear two tunics.

decisions.choice: to show his horror
decisions.reason: Readable explains the act.

records.source: ἠκούσατε τῆς βλασφημίας· τί ὑμῖν φαίνεται;
records.gloss: You heard the blasphemy; what to you does it appear?
pieces: You heard the blasphemy for yourselves. What is your verdict?"

L.64: You have heard the blasphemy. What does it seem to you?"

R.64: You heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say this terrible thing against God. What do you think we should do?"

decisions.choice: blasphemy: speech that insults God or claims what belongs to God
decisions.reason: The law punished one who cursed God's name (Leviticus 24:16). Mark does not say what made Jesus' words blasphemy. Most likely it was his claim to sit at God's right hand.

decisions.choice: what does it seem to you?: what is your judgment?
decisions.reason: The high priest asks the council for its verdict.

decisions.choice: say this terrible thing against God
decisions.reason: Readable says what blasphemy is.

records.source: οἱ δὲ πάντες κατέκριναν αὐτὸν ἔνοχον εἶναι θανάτου.
records.gloss: And all condemned him to be deserving of death.
pieces: Every one of them condemned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserved to die.

L.64: And they all condemned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as deserving death.

R.64: All of them said that Jesus was guilty and should be put to death.

decisions.choice: deserving of death: liable to the death penalty
decisions.reason: They judge him guilty of a crime that carries death. The council then hands him to Pilate (15:1), since the Romans kept the power to execute.

decisions.choice: all: all who were present
alternatives: every member of the council without exception
decisions.reason: Mark says all, but Joseph of Arimathea, a council member, was waiting for God's kingdom (15:43). Luke 23:51 says he had not agreed with their decision.

records.source: καὶ ἤρξαντό τινες ἐμπτύειν αὐτῷ καὶ περικαλύπτειν αὐτοῦ τὸ πρόσωπον καὶ κολαφίζειν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγειν αὐτῷ· Προφήτευσον, καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ῥαπίσμασιν αὐτὸν ἔλαβον.
records.gloss: And began some to spit on him and to cover of him the face and to strike him and to say to him, Prophesy, and the officers with slaps him received.
pieces: Some of them started spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They covered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face, punched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and taunted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Prophesy!" The guards, too, took charge of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with open hands.

L.65: And some began to spit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and to cover {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and to strike {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with fists and to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Prophesy!" And the officers received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with slaps.

R.65: Then some people began to spit on Jesus. They covered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could not see. They hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists and said, "Prophesy! Show us {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a prophet!" Then the guards took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and slapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: Prophesy!: a mocking test, while his own prophecy comes true
decisions.reason: With his face covered, they dare him to name who struck him (Luke 22:64). At that very hour Peter is fulfilling Jesus' prophecy of 14:30 in the courtyard below.

decisions.choice: spitting and striking: an echo of Isaiah 50:6
decisions.reason: The servant says, "I did not hide my face from shame and spitting." Jesus foretold this in 10:34.

decisions.choice: received him with slaps: took him and beat him
decisions.reason: The phrase means they took charge of him with blows.

decisions.choice: received, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts have verbs meaning they struck or threw him. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: so that he could not see; Show us you are a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable explains the point of the covering and of the taunt.

records.source: Καὶ ὄντος τοῦ Πέτρου κάτω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ ἔρχεται μία τῶν παιδισκῶν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον θερμαινόμενον ἐμβλέψασα αὐτῷ λέγει· Καὶ σὺ μετὰ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ ἦσθα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ·
records.gloss: And being Peter below in the courtyard comes one of the servant girls of the high priest, \v 67 and having seen Peter warming himself, having looked at him she says, And you with the Nazarene were, Jesus.
pieces: Meanwhile Peter was below in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came along,
and when she noticed Peter warming himself, she studied his face and said, "You, too, were with the man from Nazareth, Jesus."

L.66: And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes,
L.67: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looks at him and says, "You too were with the Nazarene, Jesus."

R.66: Peter was still down in the yard. A young woman who served the high priest came there.
R.67: She saw Peter warming himself by the fire. She looked closely at him and said, "You were with Jesus, the man from Nazareth."

decisions.choice: servant girl: a young female slave or servant of the household
decisions.reason: The word was used of a young woman who served in a house, often a slave. Such a girl kept the door (John 18:16-17).

decisions.choice: below: the council met in a room above the courtyard
decisions.reason: Mark pictures the hearing upstairs while Peter waits in the courtyard below.

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: The name says where Jesus came from (1:9, 1:24). In her mouth it may sound scornful of a man from a small Galilean village.

decisions.choice: having looked at him: she looked hard at him
decisions.reason: The verb means to fix one's eyes on someone.

records.heading: Peter denies knowing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων· Οὔτε οἶδα οὔτε ἐπίσταμαι σὺ τί λέγεις, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω εἰς τὸ προαύλιον καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν.
records.gloss: But he denied saying, Neither I know nor understand you what say. And he went out outside into the forecourt; and a rooster crowed.
pieces: But Peter denied it: "I have no idea what you are talking about; I do not understand you." Then he went out to the entrance, and a rooster crowed.

L.68: But he denied [it], saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.

R.68: But Peter said that was not true. He said, "I do not know what you are talking about. I do not understand you." Then Peter went out to the entrance of the yard. Just then a rooster crowed.

decisions.choice: and a rooster crowed, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts do not have these words. They fit Jesus' words about a rooster crowing twice (14:30, 14:72), which those manuscripts also lack in part. The SBLGNT includes them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: I neither know nor understand what you are saying
alternatives: I neither know nor understand. What are you saying?
decisions.reason: The words can be split into a denial and a question. Either way Peter pretends not to understand her.

decisions.choice: forecourt: the entrance passage or gateway into the courtyard
alternatives: a porch at the front of the house
decisions.reason: The word means the area in front of the courtyard, the gateway. Peter moves away from the light of the fire.

decisions.choice: denied: said it was not so
decisions.reason: This is the first of the three denials Jesus foretold in 14:30.

records.source: καὶ ἡ παιδίσκη ἰδοῦσα αὐτὸν ἤρξατο πάλιν λέγειν τοῖς παρεστῶσιν ὅτι Οὗτος ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐστιν.
records.gloss: And the servant girl having seen him began again to say to those standing by that This [one] of them is.
pieces: The servant girl caught sight of him there and started saying again to the people standing around, "He is one of them."

L.69: And the servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing by, "This [man] is one of them."

R.69: The servant girl saw him there. She began to tell the people standing around, "This man is one of Jesus' followers!"

decisions.choice: the servant girl: the same girl as in 14:66
decisions.reason: The article points back to the girl already named. Matthew 26:71 speaks of another girl; the Gospels tell the scene in slightly different ways.

decisions.choice: one of them: one of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: She tells the bystanders that Peter belongs to Jesus' band.

decisions.choice: one of Jesus' followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are.

records.source: ὁ δὲ πάλιν ἠρνεῖτο.
records.gloss: But again he was denying.
pieces: Again he denied it.

R.70: Again Peter said it was not true.

decisions.choice: he was denying: he kept denying
decisions.reason: The tense may show that he denied it more than once to those standing by. This is the second denial.

records.source: καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν πάλιν οἱ παρεστῶτες ἔλεγον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖος εἶ καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὁμοιάζει·
records.gloss: And after a little again those standing by were saying to Peter, Truly of them you are, also for a Galilean you are, and the speech of you is like.
pieces: A little later the bystanders again said to Peter, "You really are one of them. You are from Galilee, after all; the way you talk gives you away."

L.70: And after a little while, again those standing by were saying to Peter, "Truly you are [one] of them, for you are also a Galilean, and your speech is like [theirs]."

R.70: A little while later, the people standing there said to Peter again, "You really are one of Jesus' followers. You are from Galilee, and you talk like people from there."

decisions.choice: a Galilean: Peter's accent marked him as from Galilee
decisions.reason: People from Galilee spoke with an accent that people in Judea could hear. Jesus and his followers were known as Galileans.

decisions.choice: and your speech is like [theirs], the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts do not have these words, which are like Matthew 26:73. The SBLGNT text includes them. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: truly: really, certainly
decisions.reason: The adverb means "surely". It is not the "amen" of Jesus' sayings.

decisions.choice: the way you talk gives you away
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense: his speech shows where he is from.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἤρξατο ἀναθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύναι ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὃν λέγετε.
records.gloss: But he began to curse and to swear that Not I know the man this whom you speak of.
pieces: Then he started calling curses down and swearing oaths: "This man you speak of, I do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.71: But he began to curse and to swear, "I do not know this man of whom you speak."

R.71: Then Peter said, "May God curse me if I am lying! I promise you, I do not know this man you are talking about!"

decisions.choice: curse: call down a curse, most likely on himself if he lies
decisions.reason: The verb means to put under a curse. Mark gives no object. It may mean Peter called a curse on himself, or even that he cursed Jesus. The first fits the oath that follows.

decisions.choice: swear: take an oath
decisions.reason: To swear was to call God as witness that one was telling the truth.

decisions.choice: this man: Peter will not even say his name
decisions.reason: Peter calls Jesus only "this man". This is the third denial.

decisions.choice: May God curse me if I am lying! I promise you
alternatives: he began to curse and to swear
decisions.reason: Readable puts the curse and the oath into words. Taking the curse as on himself follows the meaning decision.

records.source: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ δευτέρου ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν· καὶ ἀνεμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τὸ ῥῆμα ὡς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι δὶς τρίς με ἀπαρνήσῃ, καὶ ἐπιβαλὼν ἔκλαιεν.
records.gloss: And immediately for a second [time] a rooster crowed. And remembered Peter the word as said to him Jesus that Before a rooster crows twice three times me you will deny; and having thrown upon he was weeping.
pieces: At that moment a rooster crowed for the second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." Then Peter broke down in tears.

L.72: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And breaking down, he was weeping.

R.72: Right then the rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before the rooster crows two times, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." Then Peter broke down and cried.

decisions.choice: having thrown upon: he broke down, he burst into tears
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw upon, and its sense here is uncertain. It may mean he set himself to weeping or broke down; or that he thought about it, as some early translations took it; or that he threw his cloak over his head. All agree that Peter wept bitterly at what he had done.

decisions.choice: he was weeping: he wept and went on weeping
decisions.reason: The tense shows weeping that went on.

decisions.choice: immediately ... a second time, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "immediately", and some important early manuscripts lack "a second time" here and "twice" in the saying, as at 14:30 and 14:68. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus' word is fulfilled
decisions.reason: Everything Jesus said in 14:30 has come true, as his words about the cup and the scattering are coming true.

decisions.choice: broke down in tears (B); broke down and cried (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the most likely sense; the footnote gives the others.
